candidate.derivedAnswer: (x^2 - y^2)/(xy), for x != 0 and y != 0; choice A.
candidate.answerReason: Substitution gives P + Q = 2x and P - Q = 2y. The expression becomes x/y - y/x = (x^2 - y^2)/(xy), with exactly the original restrictions x != 0 and y != 0.

methods.label: Simplify the substituted sums first
methods.explanation:
The sums and differences of \(P\) and \(Q\) simplify immediately:
\[
P+Q=(x+y)+(x-y)=2x,
\]
\[
P-Q=(x+y)-(x-y)=2y.
\]
The original denominators must be nonzero, so \(x\ne0\) and \(y\ne0\). On this domain, substitute and then use the common denominator \(xy\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{P+Q}{P-Q}-\frac{P-Q}{P+Q}
&=\frac{2x}{2y}-\frac{2y}{2x}\\
&=\frac{x}{y}-\frac{y}{x}\\
&=\frac{x^2-y^2}{xy}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the equivalent expression is \(\boxed{\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{xy}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
